Grove Racing details catastrophic Payne engine failure

By Connor O'Brien
25 August 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:37
Instaread

A MAJOR valvetrain failure was the catalyst for Matt Payne’s Repco Sprint Cup heartbreak.

That’s the revelation from Grove Racing, which has provided an update via a social media video featuring head of performance Alistair McVean.

Payne was cruising towards the Sprint Cup title until being forced to retire from the Sunday race at the Ipswich Super440, leaving him to instead watch on as Broc Feeney pounced.

“We were able to go out to Triple Eight last night – as they were pulling apart the engine, they kindly invited us into their shop to have a look and we’ve been able to discover there was a major mechanical failure within the valvetrain of the engine,” said McVean.

1:64 Scale TrackStars 2023 Adelaide 500 Winner #19 Ford Mustang Matt Payne Model
$29.95

“So unfortunately once that happened, there was no chance of proceeding any further, so there was nothing we could have done to have prevented it from happening or to get us back out on track at that stage.

“Obviously that was quite heartbreaking on Sunday to have that happen to us.

“We got the group together, we all sort of sat down and debriefed for a couple of hours at the pub and now we have fully reset ourselves and we’re out here at the test day, all eyes forward to the enduros, having another red-hot crack at Bathurst and the Enduro Cup. And then looking ahead to finals where we’re well placed with both drivers.”

Both the #19 and #26 Penrite Fords ran today at the Queensland Raceway test, with mileage being shared between primaries Payne and Kai Allen and their respective co-drivers Will Davison and Tim Slade.
